correctness.rationale: For each of all 455 possible inputs, the dual cover is >=1, as proved by the three exhaustive run-type cases and checked independently by two deletion-output representations. Exactly 78 nonadjacent-pair outputs receive 1/3, 13 adjacent-pair outputs receive 2/3, and 7 selected triple outputs receive 1/3; sum is 37. The standalone verifier reads and checks 37 distinct codewords and confirms disjoint deletion-descendant sets. This proves both global upper and constructive lower bounds for the exact scope.

originality.rationale: The full ISIT 2012 constant-weight primary paper and the 2012 arXiv extension establish optimal colorings and an asymptotic construction, not the precise independence number of the 15/3 graph. Its 13 modified-VT color classes each contain 35 words, whereas the new 37-word witness and 37 fractional-transversal proof determine the maximum. The separate 2012 upper-bound work supplies a general LP-duality method, but its theorems do not state or imply the sharp 15/3 integer optimum without the new specialized dual and matching construction. Public searches and published records located no identical count. Earlier unindexed work remains a risk.

value.rationale: Constant-composition deletion-code independence numbers are natural exact invariants determining how many fixed-composition messages withstand a deleted symbol. At the standard length 15 and sparse weight three, the complete exact answer of 37 is genuinely stronger than the 35-word classes from a known optimal coloring: chromatic optimality fails to capture maximum code size. The matching rational certificate is a substantive structural obstruction, not just a numerical heuristic. This finite parameter-specific fact gives a reproducible benchmark for refined deletion-code constructions and LP bounds.
